Through rigorous experimentation and diverse agricultural datasets, it is demonstrated that the incremental approach consistently outperform than traditional methods in terms of predictive accuracy metrics such as Mean absolute error (MAE), Root mean squared error (RMSE), and R-squared ($\mathrm{R}^{2}$).Findings reveal that the incremental rank-based feature selection technique not only enhances predictive accuracy ($\mathrm{MAE}=0.245, \mathrm{RMSE}=0.313, \mathrm{R}^{2}=0.878$) but also significantly reduces computational complexity. The proposed method exhibits a runtime efficiency of 8.0 seconds, making it suitable for real-time decision-making. By iteratively selecting the most informative features, the method improves model interpretability and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Smart DC Microgrid System for Renewable Energy Integration using IoT and Real-Time Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research discusses about the design and execution of a direct current (DC) microgrid system that leverages Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The microgrid combines various green energy sources, including solar panels, a wind turbine, and a DC generator, along with a battery storage unit. A microcontroller serves as the core control unit, controlling and regulating power flow. The system gives real-time data collection for performance study through IoT integration. The collected data reveals the effectiveness of the DC microgrid system, with solar energy presenting as the most reliable renewable source. The application of IoT-based control indicates the promise for intelligent and sustainable energy management. This study paves the way for advancements in microgrid technology, merging artificial intelligence, wireless energy harvesting for improved performance and peer-to-peer energy sharing.

articleTitle: From Pages to Panels: Deep Learning-based Comics Segmentation with CNN+RF
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research study employs a dual approach that involves RF and CNN to present a new means of detecting comic panels to access the education. The main objective therefore is to enhance the panel recognition and the precision of the same to aid in the preservation, searching as well and retrieval of the comics. A CNN is applied to extract features underlying the image and an RF model is applied under the classification step. From the results of our tests, we observe significant increases compared to baseline methods, the best of which is the suggested CNN+ RF with a 92.5% accuracy rate. Through this method, the capacity increases for organizing digital comic collections deftly as it furnishes a good response concerning the contingency and challenge of comic panels.

articleTitle: Enhanced ResNet-101 Model for Effective Classification of Covid-19 Disease from CXR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The recent spread of covid-19 (Corona virus) turned out as a deadliest outbreak in human history, infecting over 636 million people world-wide and claiming an estimated 6.6 million lives. With such a deadly disease spreading around the world at such a fast pace, identification of the covid-19 affected personnel is vital against the spreading of the disease and recovery of the infected individuals. Numerous mechanisms have come forth for covid-19 detection in infected patients. One such method is employing Deep Learning (DL) strategies. Supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised models can be built using DL, a subclass of Machine Learning (ML). Artificial neural networks served as inspiration for this. DL can extract features in a hierarchical manner from the data, i.e., low-level feature extraction is done first, followed by mid-level features, and high-level feature extraction is done last. This work expresses the need of DL techniques to apply on Chest Radiograph (CXR) images for effectively identifying the Covid19 infection.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Random Forest, XGBoost, and SVC Models for Fire Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Both natural and man-made ecosystems continue to face a significant fire risk, necessitating effective detection and prevention measures. The early detection of fire can be detected using various ML models. The detection of fire through ML models involves data collection, preparation, model creation, and performance evaluation. Three models were analyzed: Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Classifier (SVC). The SVC demonstrated an accuracy rate of ${9 5 \%}$, while Random Forest and XGBoost achieved near-perfect accuracy. The results highlight the effectiveness of AI-driven techniques in early fire detection, showing great potential for real-world applications and improved safety protocols through automated insights. Future research will focus on refining these models for large-scale real-world deployment.

articleTitle: NAARI- A Portable Sanitary Napkin Vending Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In an effort to address the challenges of menstrual hygiene management in developing countries, a portable sanitary pad vending machine was developed. The vending machine is powered by an Arduino Uno microcontroller and a power source that ranges between 5 to 12 volts. It features an liquid-crystal display (LCD) keypad, token acceptor with an Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) scanner for validation, and a L298d motor driver that powers two DC Servo motors to turn the spring coil system that delivers the sanitary pads or disposable bags to the user. The entire system is enclosed in a metal box for protection against damage. The LCD keypad serves as an input and output device, displaying information about the vending machine and providing instructions for its use. With the token acceptor and RFID scanner, only authorized users are granted access to the vending machine. The scanner reads the user’s RFID card, which has a unique identification number, to confirm their authorization. The portable vending machine is designed to be cost-effective and easy to use, providing an innovative solution to menstrual hygiene management challenges. It is also portable and can be relocated to various locations. Overall, the vending machine serves as a critical resource in promoting menstrual hygiene and addressing the challenges that come with it. Its use ensures that individuals have access to essential sanitary products that they need to live healthy lives.

articleTitle: AI based Compact Controller for Wind farms Economical Operation, Control and Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In India, 42.6 GW power is generated by wind turbine generators for supplying electricity to the load. Permanent Magnet DC generator, Synchronous generator and Induction generator are the most commonly used generators in the wind mill. Though the generators are designed for producing the power with maximum efficiency, monitoring, operation and control of wind mill plays an important role. The instantaneous faults like open circuit fault and least resistance fault can be easily detected and removed by the protection scheme. But the inter turn fault, core saturation condition, loss of dielectric due to ageing of machines cannot be detected until the fault occurs. The economic operation of the wind mill is based on the fault detection and prediction, uninterrupted operation of the wind mill, monitoring of parameters from the remote location. The AI based compact controller R04CPU with remote I/O module is used to monitor, control the windmill and ensures the economic operation/fault detection.

articleTitle: AI iQ-F Controller based Control of Power Factor in Power System Operating with Different Sources and Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The quality of any load is decided by its power consumption and PF (power factor). For resistive load, the pf is always unity, and it is less than unity if the connected load is inductive or capacitive load. Nowadays, Industries are mainly focusing to control the power quality issues like mitigation of other than fundamental or multiple frequency components and maintaining the pf irrespective of the load. Today APFC (Automatic Power Factor Correcting) is used for correcting the power factor from lagging to unity. But the drawback of APFC is that uses the fixed bank of capacitors. Due to the fixed bank size capacitors, the desired value of power factors is not maintained at all the time. Smoothening control of power factor is not achieved in the conventional APFC method. If the connected sources are exceedingly more than one, then it is difficult to sense the input current and phase angle values from each phase. In ordered to overcome the above-mentioned drawbacks, the AI compact controller-based power factor control method is introduced. AI compact controller uses the high-speed Input and Outputs which senses the current without any measuring delay. The phase angle is accurately measured by this compact controller. The fixed inductor and capacitor bank are converted into the dynamic inductor and capacitive bank by installing the power electronics switches like IGBT. By controlling the PWM pulses applied to the IGBT, the effective value of L and C are controlled. Thereby, the amount of magnetizing power fed into the system or grid is controlled.

Author Keywords: AI Algorithm for controlling L and C value
IGBT based control of L and C bank

articleTitle: Dynamic Treatment Strategies: The RL-CNN Model in Personalized Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Personalized medicine offers the potential to revolutionize healthcare by customizing treatments to individual patient characteristics. This study proposes a novel Reinforcement Learning-Convolutional Neural Network (RLCNN) hybrid model to optimize personalized treatment schedules, specifically focusing on medication dosage and timing. The RL-CNN model was trained on a comprehensive dataset of patient information, including medical history, demographics, and treatment outcomes. The model demonstrated superior performance compared to a baseline model, achieving significant improvements in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The application of the RL-CNN model led to enhanced dosage accuracy and schedule adherence among various patient populations. This suggests that the model can effectively provide personalized treatment plans, potentially leading to improved therapeutic outcomes and patient quality of life. This research highlights the potential of AI-driven approaches to revolutionize personalized medicine. By incorporating advanced machine learning techniques, healthcare providers can make more informed decisions and deliver more effective treatments.

articleTitle: CampusConnect: A Collaborative College Hub for Reselling and Sharing Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: CampusConnect is an innovative online platform designed to enhance the college experience by providing a unified space for social networking, knowledge sharing, and financial transactions. This study aims to evaluate the impact of CampusConnect on student engagement, knowledge sharing, and community building. A mixedmethods approach, combining quantitative and qualitative research, was employed to assess the effectiveness of the platform. Survey results indicate high levels of student satisfaction with CampusConnect’s functionality, with active participation in buying and selling, discussions, and resource sharing. The study highlights the positive impact of CampusConnect on academic engagement, financial literacy, and fostering a sense of belonging within the university community. Additionally, it identifies areas for future improvement, such as enhancing usability, customization options, and integration with existing educational systems. CampusConnect has emerged as a valuable tool that supports student learning, promotes community engagement, and prepares students for lifelong learning in the digital age.

articleTitle: Advanced Chicken Disease Detection with Keras and TensorFlow Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Convolutional Neural Networks in spotting diseases in images of chickens. The model, examining a set of chicken pictures, achieved an overall 98.27% accuracy. The CNN model perfected using TensorFlow Achieved Keras had excellent performance measures against types of diseases in terms of Precision, Recall, and F1-Score. In other words, the model is a resource that can assist a poultry farmer in determining diseases like coccidiosis, Newcastle Disease, and Salmonella. Early detection and management of chicken diseases are vital to maintaining healthy poultry. These old methods are cumbersome, time-inefficient, and require unique and valuable expertise. The research problem is conceived in the development of a CNN model that can automatically detect diseases with the best elevation in the accuracy and effectiveness of the disease identification process amid poultry. Diagnosing diseases using these methods in chickens can be highly difficult and precise, thereby challenging the farmers in this industry.

articleTitle: Classification Model for Meticulous Presaging Heart disease Results for sarcopenic LRMM and CA calcification in healthy adults using Machine learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Sarcopenic obesity, a condition characterized by both muscle loss and excess body fat, is a significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease. This study aims to develop a machine learning model to predict the risk of sarcopenic obesity and heart disease. A dataset comprising 3050 patients aged 66 years and older was obtained from the UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository. The dataset includes relevant attributes such as BMI, protein intake, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), fat percentage, age, complete blood count (CBC), chest pain, sex, and more. Several machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression, were employed to build the prediction model. The model’s performance was evaluated based on its accuracy in identifying individuals at risk of sarcopenic obesity and heart disease. The results of this study demonstrate the potential of machine learning in early disease detection and prevention. By accurately predicting the risk of sarcopenic obesity and heart disease, healthcare providers can implement timely interventions and improve patient outcomes..

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Heart Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Heart disease remains to be a foremost universal health issue, highlighting the need for precise and effective predictive tools to support early diagnosis and timely intervention. This work presents an $\mathbf{A I} / \mathbf{M L}$ prediction system designed to detect heart diseases by comparing and evaluating multiple machine learning algorithms. The proposed system utilizes a comprehensive dataset that includes a variety of patient attributes such as demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors, gathered from multiple healthcare sources. Through preprocessing and feature engineering, the dataset is organized for training and testing the machine learning models. To achieve accurate predictions, this work appraises the efficiency of some prevalent ML algorithms, including decision trees, random forests, logistic regression, Bayes, support vector machines, and k-nearest neighbors. A thorough comparative analysis is conducted, assessing the algorithms based on significant scientific metrics such as recall, accuracy, F1-score, precision and AUC-ROC, to determine their suitability for heart disease prediction.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Smart Security Camera System using YOLO Algorithm in Security Setting
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The proposed Deep Learning based Smart Security Camera System using Yolo Algorithm in Security Setting is designed to detect unusual behavior, like someone covering their face entirely, and responding to that by generating a beep sound to alert. Unlike older systems, it doesn’t just record incidents for later review it can recognize problems as it happens and take action right away. Even if someone wears a full face mask, this system notes them and raise an alarm immediately. It works by using an efficient algorithm called YOLO (You Only Look Once) to quickly know what’s happening in the live camera footage. That is, it can spot multiple objects in real time without slowing down. Overall, this security system is a step ahead in keeping areas safer. It is faster, as it can react to potential threats without needing as many human interventions.

articleTitle: Various Methods to Diagnose the Faults Occurring in Photovoltaics System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: An investigation of solar panel failure detection is presented in this research work. Solar panels are a significant source of renewable energy, and the effective production of electricity depends on their optimal operation. Unfortunately, they are susceptible to flaws for a few reasons, including wear and tear, manufacturing flaws, and environmental variables. Faults can cause the panel to operate less efficiently, provide less energy, or possibly fail entirely. Early issue identification is therefore crucial for prompt maintenance and repair, which can stop additional damage and ensure that the solar panel performs at its best. This study examines several methodologies, including electrical and thermal imaging techniques, machine learning algorithms, and fault detection in solar panels. These methods are ranked according to how well they work at finding various solar panel defects and how easily they can be used. This proposed method compares various fault detection techniques used in solar photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Severity-Level Classification of Alzheimer’s Disease from MRI Scans using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Effective diagnosis and monitoring of Alzheimer’s relies increasingly on advanced imaging techniques such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). The work in this paper focuses on the application of Convolutional Neural Networks in classifying the stages of this Alzheimer’s disease with the MRI data. In this paper, the used dataset consists of 6400 MRI images, which are basically segmented classification of four categories: Mild Demented, Moderate Demented, Non-Demented, and Very Mild Demented. The data was divided into training, testing, and validation sets to rigorously evaluate the CNN model’s performance. The accuracy of the developed CNN model was 99% overall. Other performance metrics it had were precision, recall, and F1-scores, all of which turned out to be at an average of 99% for the different classes. For perfect classification in the Moderate Demented category, these results describe the high efficacy of CNNs in accurately differentiating between stages of various dementias. The dataset distribution contains 3,200 non-demented images, 896 Mild Demented, 64 Moderate Demented, and 2,240 Very Mild Demented. This success of the classification model in predicting Alzheimer’s disease stages underlines its potential to increase automated diagnostic tools. The work contributes with value to the field, providing a framework that can be reliably used for MRI-based Alzheimer’s classification and lays a foundation for further work in automated disease detection and monitoring.

articleTitle: A CNN-RF Hybrid Model for Cross View Gait Recognition Method using CASIA-B Cross
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Many advancements in human Gait have been made so far in the research field which have even been implemented to a greater extent. Gait recognition has proved to be much more compatible as compared to other biometric processes. Currently, cross-view gait identification techniques disregard the possible dynamical information of the gait sequences and always create representations for recognition from different deep convolutional networks. If pedestrians possess distinct gait patterns, gait recognition may be executed by the computation of their dynamic properties from every perspective. The problem of cross-view gait detection is difficult because variations in perspective can significantly affect the silhouettes of gaits. Deep learning advancements have raised the bar for cross-view gait identification performance. However, the scarcity of gait samples from various viewpoints limits the effectiveness of the deep learning-based cross-view gait detection techniques now in use. This paper uses the methodology provided in Deep Learning algorithms through CNN and Random Forest. After the role played by different layers in CNN, a strong classification is performed by Random forests by detecting a strong probability based on more than one decision tree. CASIA B Gait dataset has been used that included 6703 subjects, from four view angles CV1, CV2, CV3, and CV4 $\left(15^{\circ}, 30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\right)$ Here the model has been used to classify gait silhouettes at Four view angles CV1, CV2, CV3, and CV4. A performance metrics have been generated as an output of the classification of the subjects. Overall Cross View Angle 2 CV2 had the maximum accuracy out of all the four view angles which is $0.98 \%$, the second highest accuracy was CV1 i.e. $0.97 \%$, CV3, and CV4 got the same value of accuracy i.e. $0.96 \%$. Furthermore, we assess several gait recognition methods that are resistant to view angle variations.

articleTitle: Crop Yield Prediction: Leveraging Machine Learning for Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: : Accurate crop yield prediction is essential for ensuring food security and optimizing agricultural practices. Traditional methods often rely on historical data and expert knowledge, which may not always be sufficient. This research explores the application of machine learning techniques to predict crop yield based on various factors such as soil properties, weather conditions, and crop management practices. By analyzing historical agricultural data, this research study aims to develop robust predictive models. The research utilizes Random Forest, a abstract- powerful machine learning algorithm to extract patterns from the data and make accurate yield predictions. The results of this study can provide valuable insights to farmers, enabling them to make informed decisions about crop selection, resource allocation, and risk management. By integrating machine learning, this research contributes to the development of sustainable agriculture practices and improves food security.

articleTitle: Automated Implementation of a TCPDUMP Solution for Network Traffic Analysis, Strengthening Digital Security in Cyberspace
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The advance of information technology gave rise to new information and communication technologies, providing a conjunctural environment to cyberspace (Internet). This constitutes the fifth domain of human interaction and every day it extends more and more, crossing entire nations and making it possible to connect us to the whole world, breaking the paradigm of borders in record time, where at the same time it is possible to host more information and providing more and more services (in the cloud). But as a result, this new interaction space has given rise to the emergence of new threats created by individuals, organizations or states that seek to take advantage of this new virtual way of interacting. Illegal activities in this medium can have very significant effects on the victim and bring substantial benefits to the perpetrator, who often cannot be identified. That is why it is necessary to counteract any type of computer threat, being necessary to analyze network traffic using the TCPDUMP technique, which interacts within a public or private network, to identify who is trying to invade your private computer space, in order to neutralize any unauthorized access. In the present work a strategy for digital security is proposed, to avoid attacks in Cyberspace that can affect an organization today. It should be noted that for this case the implementation of a network will be carried out, which allows the connection in a secure way.

articleTitle: OralGuard: Harnessing Inception-ResNet-v2 for Cutting-Edge Oral Health Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This paper considers the application of the InceptionResNetV2 architecture in the classification of pathologies of the mouth. Six classes are focused on: calculus, caries, ulcers, gingivitis, discoloration of tooth enamel, and hypodontia. The performance of the model is benchmarked on a set containing 1166 labeled images, taking into account the prevalence and severity of each condition. The results indicate that, among all of the scenarios, InceptionResNetV2 has achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 3 \%}$. Accuracy in distinguishing classes: calculus, 0.76; caries, 0.99; ulcers, 1.00; gingivitis, 0.79; discoloration of tooth, 0.99; and hypodontia, 0.99. Its macro average for precision, recall, and F1-score are 0.91, 0.92, and 0.91, respectively. The results showed that the InceptionResNetV2 model could differentiate between classes for a variety of common oral pathologies, thus being able to be very helpful in improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in dental practice. Further studies are required to confirm generalizability of these results to larger and more diverse datasets and to real-world clinical settings.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Fraud Detection in the Financial Services Sector: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Financial Fraud Detection is essential for securing financial transactions and mitigating fraudulent activities. This paper explores various fraud types, such as payment fraud and account takeover fraud, highlighting the urgency due to online payment fraud projected to exceed ${\$}$ 343 billion by 2027. We discuss methodologies like Machine Learning, Behavioral Analytics, Anomaly Detection, and Data Analytics for detecting fraud. Using a synthetic dataset of mobile money transactions, we evaluated three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). While Logistic Regression struggled with imbalanced data, the Decision Tree showed balanced performance with better precision and recall. The MLP, though precise, had lower recall, missing significant fraud cases. These findings emphasize the need to fine-tune models for effective fraud detection. This research identifies threats in financial security and proposes adaptive strategies to protect businesses and consumers in a digital financial landscape.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Tree-Cutting Activities in Forest Environments using Convolutional Neural Networks and Advanced Audio Feature Extraction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Detecting tree cutting is essential in preventing illegal logging and also conserving the forest’s natural resources. This research aimed to present a solution for illegal logging by developing a sound detection system capable of identifying tree-cutting activities in forest environments. Based on concepts of machine learning and deep learning techniques, this research introduced a customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model that is used to classify different sound events related to tree cutting. The model is trained using a dataset of four classes, and each class of 1200 samples are chainsaws, axe cutting, and handsaw sounds, along with other sounds of the forest environment. In this model features extracted from sound samples such as MFCC, Mel-Spectrogram, and Tonnetz are to enhance the model’s classification accuracy. The proposed model with customized CNN architecture provided the classification accuracy of $\mathbf{8 2 \%}$ over the 4800 sample of the dataset.

articleTitle: Indian Sign Language Classification using Deep Convolutional Neural Network with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The Indian Sign Language (ISL) classification model uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and analysis with Transfer Learning technology to understand ISL gestures by deaf people. This process entails categorizing hand signals into thirty-five groups, which comprise digits 1-9 (9) and alphabets A-Z (26). The developed model is a great support for people who want to know what the deaf say. The ultimate aim of this project is to categorize ISL Gestures into 35 distinct categories. These divisions are made using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). To achieve higher accuracy in classification, various transfer learning models such as ResNet50, Xception, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB5 and VGG19 were used in this study. Consequently, ResNet50 achieves an accuracy of 99.96%, Xception at 27.15%, DenseNet121 at 77.94%, and EfficientNetB5 at 50.93%.

articleTitle: Low-cost System to Characterize the Movement of the Peruvian Paso Horse by Inertial Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In these times, information and communication technology is within the reach of many disciplines for its use and exploitation, in this sense find devices that can evaluate the behavior of movement, with the intention of recognizing certain patterns, in this work present a low cost system to begin the evaluation and characterization of movement in the Peruvian Paso horse. The Peruvian Paso horse is characterized by its body structure and by the shape of its flat gait, evidenced in the particularity of the movement of its limbs, which gives the sensation that it is dancing. The work with an inertial sensor based on an accelerometer located in the horse’s center of gravity. As a result, the present the movement recorded in the X, Y and Z axes. The records presented are the first results in the procedure of biomechanical characterization of the Peruvian Paso horse, in the conclusions present some recommendations to increase the biomechanical variables and characteristics.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Waterbodies from Otsu’s Preprocessed Satellite Images using VGG-UNet
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Automatic monitoring of the water-bodies from Satellite Image (SI) is a common process to monitor water reservoir and its impact on the ecological change. When the necessary image is recorded, it is then examined using a chosen imaging scheme to detect the availability of the water and how it can be used in future for a selected application. This research aims to propose and implement a method for automatic segmentation and evaluation of the water region from the chosen SI. In this work, 2000 images/mask is considered to execute the automatic segmentation using pretrained deeplearning models and the performance is confirmed using the raw- and Otsu’s thresholded-image. The experimental outcome of this study is executed on $512 \times 512 \times 3$ pixel sized images and the achieved result confirms that the VGG19-UNet based approach provides a better outcome compared to other models chosen in this study. Further, the result by the Otsu’s processed image is better compared to the raw-image and in future, it can be considered to other SI examination task.

articleTitle: Analysis of Machine Learning based Financial Planning Applications in Online Digital Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The society has developed and science and technology have advanced. Financial Robot is a crucial application product in the corporate financial management process automation development process. Financial managers can be efficiently replaced by financial robots to undertake some extremely repetitious. Now that we are in the information age, advanced technology has also been used to the financial sector. Robot process automation employing artificial intelligence technology has been implemented, and customized programs have been written for financial machines. Enterprises today need to make sure that their financial work is developing smoothly if they want to succeed in the market competition. The internal control of businesses can benefit clearly from financial robots. At the same time, businesses incorporate financial robots into their basic financial departments, which may easily maintain the privacy of their internal financial data through data control. Financial robots can increase financial management efficiency, cut labor expenses to some extent, lessen the security risks and error issues brought on by repetitive manual tasks, and ultimately.

articleTitle: Low-cost sytem for monitoring and damage assessment of natural disasters
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Global warming is affecting most of the countries, with more emphasis on those that are on the coasts of the Pacific Ocean, as is the case of Peru, where the warming of the sea waters is occurring more frequently, which causes a considerable increase in rainfall, causing mainly the overflow of rivers. In order to provide assistance to the affected population, various information is required, ranging from satellite images of the different space missions, to know the effect in general, as well as images of the river areas and the affected population, in order to make decisions related to the aid to be provided. In the present work, developed a low cost system to organize the information coming from the different media, by means of the configuration of a storage system “NASS”, a platform can be organized for the loading and unloading of diverse images, videos or information that is considered important for the evaluation of the damages, this system is found in lines so that it has access in real time, The system allows to configure access, create profiles for people in the affected areas where they can show the help they require, as well as information of collaborating entities where they can provide information that can mitigate the effects of these phenomena, the proposal can be used and scaled to different situations that are considered emergency.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Antenna Parameter Optimization in Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Communication technology in recent days has undergone rapid growth and the need to improve the performance of antennas has also got its equal importance. The inclusion of the optimization methods satisfies the need to increase performance. In this paper, the inset-fed rectangular patch antenna is optimized using Deep learning along with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The neural network is trained using the datasets and PSO is adapted to optimize the antenna parameters. The output from the neural network is the relationship between the model parameters and the antenna parameters. The antenna designed from the neural networks output is found to have best performance in terms of directivity, gain, efficiency, and miniaturization. The simulated results show that the antenna has a 24% reduction in size and a 70% improvement in efficiency and is used for applications in the 5.8 GHz (ISM band).

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Assessment: AI-Powered Evaluation with RAG and LLM Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The world of Artificial Intelligence is rapidly evolving after the introduction of GEN AI. Artificial Intelligence is being adopted in many fields and to automate complex works which frees up humans to something better. In the field of education, Artificial Intelligence is used in various ways, to tailor the content to meet the needs of individual students, one to one tutoring experience, as teaching assistant, in planning, content development. The scope AI and its subfield can be leveraged further, and it is possible to use it for exam assessment, use the data from Student Management System to generate some meaningful insight on Students behavior, discipline, attendance etc. Natural Language Processing, a subset of Artificial Intelligence can be combined with other AI subsets like Large Language Model to facilitate the Teacher, Parents and Students interaction, Parents can use chatBots to receive candid feedback of their kid’s performance, to generate relative performance improvement compared to previous cycle, suggestion for improvement. All it takes is to connect the Artificial Intelligence subsets with some reference system like Students database. This research analysis is to evaluate student’s performance and provide feedback factoring based on four main areas like exam answer sheet, practicals, attendance and assignments. This research provides technical implementation and guidance to implement the solution using the Retrieval Augmented Generation and Large Language Model, and an architectural overview of combining data from various input modes like student information from Student Management System, text book, digital answer sheet and embedding them in the Vector database.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Detection of PCOS using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a widespread endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age, frequently resulting in infertility due to hormonal abnormalities. Symptoms include severe acne, irregular menstrual cycles, excess body hair, and weight gain. Early and accurate diagnosis of PCOS is critical for effective management and minimizing related health risks. Traditional manual identification of ovarian follicles in ultrasound images by radiologists can lead to misdiagnoses. To overcome this, proposed an innovative PCOS classification approach that integrates the encoder part of a Transformer model with various pretrained CNN models for robust feature extraction from ultrasound images. This hybrid model leverages advanced deep learning and attention mechanisms to significantly improve diagnostic precision. Our study aims to deliver a highly accurate and comprehensive PCOS detection method, enabling early intervention and customized treatment plans. This cutting-edge approach, situated at the intersection of artificial intelligence and women’s health, holds the potential to transform PCOS management and enhance healthcare outcomes, representing a notable advancement in the field.

articleTitle: A study on Efficiency of Bio Medical Data Extraction from PubMed Dataset using Elastic Search Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Modern software applications rely heavily on search and analytics as crucial components. Extracting valuable information from big data records is mandatory for development of effective text mining models. Existing text mining models require large number of trained data but lagging due to the small datasets available. For information extraction from the literature, there is a growing need for precise text mining methods. This research study provides an idea of extracting required information from the literature and identify research trends with the help of elastic search. People can better understand life’s phenomena and its rules on biological knowledge with aid of elastic search.

articleTitle: Analyzing Weather Impact on Crop Prices
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Changes in crop prices are quite common everywhere irrespective of the location. These changes are often driven by various factors such as climatic conditions, market dynamics (demand and supply), government schemes, etc. Crop price prediction has several important purposes such as risk management and market planning. Crops are very essential for numerous reasons like food security, Trade, economic growth, ecosystem sustainability, etc. These crops encompass the health of the ecosystem. Accurate prediction of crop price plays a major role in supply chain market management, market stability, and global trade. To make an accurate crop price prediction, Deep-learning models were tested and trained with the data collected from the market. This data contains five different crops (onion, potato, apple, brinjal, orange), rainfall, temperature, wind, and humidity are the important parameters considered for this prediction. Multilayer Perceptron (MLPs), Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and LongShort Term Memory (LSTM) are different deep learning models that were tested and trained in this work.

articleTitle: Image Steganography with Dual Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In today’s world, the biggest problem is storing digital information securely. The data may be stolen or hacked by anyone at any time. So, to solve this problem there is a way called cryptography and steganography. This work mainly includes steganography and its implementation in securing the messages that must be sent. This work primarily focuses on image steganography which helps the sender to store the information in the images. This work also includes F5 steganography, which is the type of steganography and the hybrid encryption methods such as AES and Blowfish algorithms.

articleTitle: A Review on Human Respiratory Model Development for Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The proposed method attempts to replicate and examine the physiological response of the respiratory system under diverse circumstances, such as respiratory illnesses, air pollution, and ventilation techniques by designing and creating a 3D printed lung model, choosing and integrating the right blowers and sensors, and testing and validating the model’s functionality are all part of the study project. The findings of this study have serious implications for respiratory health and medical research since they offer a practical and affordable method to imitate respiratory physiology.

articleTitle: Autonomous Line Follower Robot with Obstacle Avoidance Design
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The evolution of the Line Following Robot starts with an analog design and advances to a refined version incorporating an Arduino Nano microcontroller and an ultrasonic sensor for obstacle avoidance. Initially, the focus was on developing a simple robot capable of following a predetermined path using basic sensor technology, specifically infrared sensors for line detection. The robot was able to differentiate between various line colours, each with distinct properties, and adjust its path accordingly. Both versions of the robot’s hardware, including motors, sensors, and motor drivers, are discussed in detail. Additionally, the software development process, essential for controlling the robot’s behaviour, is thoroughly examined. The robot’s versatility points to its applicability across various domains, including commercial, industrial, medical, and educational settings, emphasizing its wide-ranging significance and potential impact.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Frame Work for Building Extraction using Fast Accurate Bilateral Filter, Fast Corner Method and Improved Gaussian Blur
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Identifying and detection of buildings from satellite imagery is beneficial in mapping, environmental training, disaster management, city planning, geo references, and studies purposes. In this paper first, Gaussian mask is used in pre-processing to avoid blurring effects in computer vision to enhance image structures at different scales then Gaussian blur smoothens irregular pixel values by excising the extreme outliers. With fast accurate bilateral filter, quality of edge preserves in buildings has been smoothened, Local key point’s extraction, dominant directions and weights were extracted to detect corners of different shaped buildings in image very quickly. Based upon weightage and correct directions in voting, Transforms applied for optimum results. We processed satellite images taken from Mumbai, Chennai cities, and Nagapattinam town and rural of Nannilam in Tamilnadu, India. Kernel density distribution become extensively utilized to find the density flow for metropolitan cities also. In results, buildings detection without shadow in 28 to 35 seconds in cities and 5 to 8 seconds in urban areas and improved accuracy of 40 % in metro and 8 % in urban than existing detection techniques.

articleTitle: Image Enhancment Hair Removal in Dermoscopy Images Using Dual Swin Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Skin cancer requires effective treatment for better survival rates especially in the case of melanoma. To reduce the image noise and removing hair the conventional method takes high computational complexity and decayed accuracy. In order to tackle this issue, an innovative dual Swin autoencoder has been proposed in this paper. This autoencoder utilizes Swin Transformer blocks to effectively eliminate noise from images and get rid of unwanted hair, all while maintaining important characteristics of the skin and lesions. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms conventional techniques, with PSNR values up to 81.71 dB and SSIM up to 0.99, effectively eliminating hair and retaining important skin features. This approach enhances the accuracy of melanoma diagnosis in dermoscopy images.

articleTitle: Plastic Litter Detection using YOLOv8 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: One of the most concerning environmental issues is water pollution, which is mostly brought on by plastic waste that is dumped into the aquatic region from land. These plastics pose a threat to the marine ecosystem’s equilibrium, the coastal communities, economic health, and their animals. This would unavoidably have an impact on aquatic and human life. Even if they work well, most widely used techniques have several drawbacks when it comes to identifying and measuring plastics. As a result, it is important to implement alternative techniques that will make it simple to recognize plastics and facilitate their removal using latest technologies. This research study utilizes the You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8 Deep Learning (DL) algorithm for object detection and identifying plastics in the surface of water bodies and gives the count of the plastics that are detected as a result.

articleTitle: Two Level Encryption Scheme for Securing Private Data Over Hybrid Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Health care data is characterized by the presence of many sensitive attributes and leakage of these sensitive attributes can breach patient’s privacy. With the rapid adoption of cloud for data storage by healthcare enterprises, it becomes necessary to secure the data from privacy breaches both directly or through inference. Recently hybrid cloud based data offloading is proposed to enhance the security of cloud. As a continuation to it, a data distribution scheme for a hybrid cloud with enhanced security and access control is proposed in this work. The proposed solution addresses multiple objectives of providing security, fine-grained access control, and differential privacy for users. A novel two level encryption algorithm is proposed as part of work to address these multiple objectives.

Author Keywords: Low complexity mutual authentication algorithm: Detecting attacks

articleTitle: Rice Leaf Disease Detection using Fusion Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Rice leaf disease detection is critical for maintaining crop yields and ensuring food security, especially in regions heavily reliant on rice cultivation. Traditional manual inspection methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to error. This study presents an advanced deep learning-based ensemble model for accurate and efficient detection of three common rice leaf diseases: hispa, brown spot, and leaf blast. The proposed approach integrates feature fusion and ensemble learning techniques to leverage the complementary strengths of ResNet and DenseNet architectures. Robust data preprocessing and augmentation strategies are employed to enhance model performance. The ensemble model achieves superior accuracy compared to individual models, demonstrating the potential of ensemble learning for rice leaf disease detection. Experimental results on a field-captured dataset of 5,678images validate the model’s effectiveness, with an accuracy of $82 \%$ in disease classification. This research contributes to the development of automated disease detection systems, supporting sustainable agricultural practices and mitigating crop losses.

Author Keywords: Ensemble. Feature Fusion (FF) ResNet (Residual Neural Network) DenseNet (Densely Connected Convolutional Network)

articleTitle: Smart Energy Metering and Load Control using GSM Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research presents a novel smart energy metering system that integrates GSM technology with energy meters to enhance energy management and consumer awareness. The system aims to address issues related to timely payment and energy consumption control. By incorporating GSM technology, the proposed system enables real-time monitoring of energy consumption and sends alerts to users when their prepaid balance is nearing depletion. Additionally, it provides remote control capabilities, allowing users to switch loads on or off remotely. The proposed system has been implemented using a hardware prototype, demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness. The results indicate that the system can significantly improve energy efficiency and reduce energy costs. This research contributes to the development of smart energy solutions that empower consumers to make informed decisions about their energy usage and promote sustainable energy practices.

Author Keywords: ’ Global System for Mobile Communication (GSM) module

articleTitle: Automatic Paneer Slicing in Dairy Industry using PLC
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The current method for slicing paneer is done manually, with workers placing paneer on a cutting surface and using knives to cut it into portions. This method is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often results in uneven slice thickness and quality. It also relies on skilled workers and can vary based on their experience and fatigue. Despite its common use, this manual process is inefficient, inconsistent, and hard to scale. To improve this, the dairy industry should consider more ergonomic workstations and specialized cutting tools to reduce worker fatigue and improve consistency. Training programs can also help workers achieve more uniform slices and better product quality. In summary, while manual slicing is still widely used, there’s a need for more efficient, consistent, and scalable methods. By investing in new technologies and training, dairy producers can enhance their slicing processes, leading to better quality products, higher productivity, and greater market competitiveness.

articleTitle: Navigating the Cloud: A Review of Emerging Trends in Security
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: From 2016 to 2023, the percentage of the world’s devices using the cloud increased from 1% to 85%. Data in the cloud is data-at-rest and data-in-transit, both subject to risks. This research study reviews the systems outlined in research, aiming to secure cloud data from imminent threats. Our analysis encompasses cutting-edge encryption protocols, intrusion detection mechanisms, and adaptive access controls. By understanding these trends, organizations can enhance their cloud infrastructure and protect sensitive information.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Medical Imaging: CNN Performance in Pneumonia Detection from X-rays
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Pneumonia is a serious infection to the respiratory system; it is also a significant health risk, more so in vulnerable populations. Early and accurate detection is paramount for effective treatment and management. In this study, we explore an application of Convolutional Neural Networks for automatized pneumonia detection from chest X-ray images. Our model is trained and evaluated using a dataset that includes 624 images, 390 images labeled as Pneumonia and 234 labeled as Normal. According to this, performance metrics indicate performance in robust capabilities of classification, with overall accuracy at 93%. The model exactly had a precision of 0.93, a recall of 0.96, and an F1-score of 0.94 in pneumonia detection and a precision of 0.92, a recall of 0.88, and an F1-score of 0.90 in the normal cases. The macro averages are 0.93 for precision, 0.92 for recall, and 0.92 for the F1 score; the weighted averages reproduced the same result. These findings prove that the CNN can be a helpful tool within a clinical set-up for timely diagnosis of pneumonia, hence doing timely medical interventions for better patient outcome.

articleTitle: Centralized Monitoring System for Street Light Fault Detection & Location Tracking using Android Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT), an evolving technological paradigm, primarily aims to interconnect devices and components, enabling communication between these entities and people. The integration of IoT for automated detection of faulty streetlights represents a significant advancement in urban infrastructure management. The project’s overarching objective is to streamline the control and identification processes related to malfunctioning streetlights. In this initiative, streetlight issues are identified through a dual approach: firstly, via resident complaints and secondly, through the monitoring of operational status using sensors. These sensors are specifically designed to evaluate streetlight functionality, providing real-time insights into their operational status. Resident complaints are seamlessly transmitted to designated personnel through a dedicated Android application, facilitating swift and efficient issue resolution. The complaints database serves as a repository, meticulously documenting the precise locations of faulty streetlights for improved logistical efficiency. Moreover, users can monitor the progress and status of their reports through the application, promoting transparency and accountability in the resolution process. Furthermore, our project also delivers real-time data on the current, voltage, and intensity of every streetlight within a designated area through an Android application. By implementing this comprehensive approach, the project aims to ensure prompt and effective resolution of identified issues, thereby enhancing community safety and well-being. Additionally, the application includes a feature allowing administrators to remotely control the lights, further enhancing convenience and control over urban lighting infrastructure.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Disease Prediction in Rice Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: It is essential to identify diseases in plants to increase crop production and yield. Therefore, prediction of these diseases at an early stage is important to avoid or minimize crop losses. In this paper we have taken the use case of rice crop and predicting diseases namely leaf smut, brown spots and bacterial leaf blight using machine learning techniques. Labeled image dataset of these three diseases in rice plants is used and several machine learning algorithms (DT, RF, KNN, GBM, LR, NB, and MobileNet) are applied on it. To compare performance of different models, calculations and analysis of confusion matrix, recall, precision and f1-score have been used.

articleTitle: Diabetic Foot-Ulcer Detection from Digital Images using ResNet Variants and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The occurrence rate of diabetes is increasing particularly in low- and middle-income countries due to various causes and it may cause mild to harsh illness. In order to control his harshness, early diagnosis and treatment is crucial. Diabetic Foot-Ulcer (DFU) is a major issue of diabetes and appropriate detection is necessary for the treatment. This work aims to detect the DFU from the digital-images using deep-learning (DL) technique. The stages in DL-scheme based DFU detection includes; digital-image collection and resizing, feature mining using a chosen ResNet-model, features selection using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), fused features vector generation using PSO selected features, and classification and verification. In this work, the digital-image based DFU detection is executed using 1050 images (525 healthy and 525 DFU) and the proposed investigation is executed using Python-software. The classification result of this study confirms that the fused-features based DFU detection offered >99% accuracy with the SoftMax-classifier. This confirms that the implemented scheme can be chosen to examine the clinically collected digital-images having the DFU.

articleTitle: Transformer Fault Identification and Classification of Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: India’s electrical distribution networks have experienced transformer failures, causing significant downtime and power supply interruptions. Prompt repair and monitoring can prevent up to 30% of transformer failures, reducing maintenance costs and downtime. Hence, in recent years, the Indian government is funding to modernize the country’s electrical infrastructure, including smart grid technology, predictive maintenance, and reliability standards. This research study focuses on transformer fault detection and classification by integrating current and voltage sensors. Utilizing machine learning techniques, specifically K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) and Random Forest (RF) algorithms, the system aims to identify and classify various faults such as short circuit, overvoltage, under voltage, high vibration and as well as normal condition. The sensors provide real-time data, which is used to train the models for accurate fault prediction. KNN leverages proximitybased classification, while RF utilizes an ensemble of decision trees to enhance accuracy. The trained models enable quick and precise identification of transformer faults, contributing to early detection and prevention of potential damage. This integrated approach utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to improve the reliability and efficiency of transformer systems in power distribution networks.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Natural Language Processing for Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Advanced sentiment analysis is crucial for modern applications as it provides deep insights into human emotions, opinions, and sentiments expressed in text. Its impact spans across various industries and domains. Staying updated with the latest methods, such as transformer-based models, is essential for improving model performance, addressing challenges, and exploring new applications. By integrating modern pretrained model systems, performance can be significantly enhanced. This research study systematically reviews the status of sentiment analysis studies nowadays, employing the PRISMA model for articles to improve the calibre of the literature review procedure. This comprehensive overview of the literature provides useful insights into research gaps and helps researchers and academia stay updated with current trends in sentiment analysis. The review of 80 peer-reviewed articles covering 2019 to 2024 reveals significant findings that can inspire further research in the sentiment study.

articleTitle: Hydroponic NFT for Brinjal cultivation using Decision Tree (DT) and K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Hydroponic brinjal cultivation with the Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) is the intended setting for this study’s evaluation of the K Nearest Neighbor (KNN) and Decision Tree (DT) algorithms. This study uses a wide range of inputs relevant to hydroponic systems to assess how well different machine learning approaches can predict brinjal growth, yield, and quality parameters. Data Collection: A wide range of environmental parameters, including pH levels, water temperatures, light exposure, and nutrient concentrations, are measured using the NFT approach. The collection also includes parameters particular to individual plants, such as yield, fruit dimensions, and leaf area. Results: It can be concluded that brinjal production and growth metrics may be predicted with an acceptable degree of accuracy using both the Decision Tree and K Nearest Neighbor algorithms. Nevertheless, in some situations, KNN is more accurate than Decision Tree, and it is also easier to interpret and execute. Conclusion: KNN predicts brinjal yield with an accuracy of 88%, while Decision Tree predicts it with an accuracy of 85%. Depending on the particular parameters being predicted, precision and recall measures change, with KNN typically displaying higher levels of precision.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wireless Sensor Network using Advanced Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research study intends to optimize the wireless sensor nodes to minimize energy consumption for improving lifespan and performance of wireless networks. To align to this objective, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) are used as optimization techniques in MATLAB, so that data is communicated to base stations with minimum energy consumption. Optimization needs fitness function which is based on energy consumption for sensor nodes and data transmission rates, moreover distance between the node and base station is also essential. With this ideology, it is conceptualized that sensor nodes are based on energy consumption, data transmission rates and distance from base station. PSO and GA algorithms inspect 12 sensor nodes network; position of node, energy level and data rate were different. Results obtained from both the optimization techniques are compared on basis of energy consumption and convergence rate.

articleTitle: Adaptive Score Normalization using Machine Learning for enhanced Fingerprint Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Fingerprint identification systems play a vital role in biometric security but are often influenced by fluctuations in scanning settings and environmental variables. The conventional normalizing techniques such as Min-Max, Z-Score, and Tanh normalization provide fixed solutions that do not adjust to these variations, therefore degrading the accuracy and resilience of the results. This study presents a machine learning-based adaptive normalization system that seamlessly adapts to present circumstances by integrating contextual information, such as ambient variables and scanner-specific features, with raw fingerprint scores. The procedure includes the gathering of data, doing preprocessing, training models using decision trees, random forests, and neural networks, and implementing dynamic normalization. Comprehensive testing conducted on several scanners and settings has shown the efficacy of this method, demonstrating substantial improvements in both recognition accuracy and resilience. Assessment measures such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score validate the higher efficacy of this adaptive approach in comparison to static methods, thereby improving operational adaptability and establishing a basis for wider biometric identification applications.

articleTitle: Traffic Analysis with Count Prediction and Speed Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Traffic congestion is a persistent issue in urban areas, significantly impacting daily life. This research proposes an intelligent traffic management system utilizing computer vision techniques to address this challenge. The system employs a Faster R-CNN model to detect and count vehicles in real-time video feeds from surveillance cameras. By analyzing traffic patterns and identifying congestion hotspots, the system can provide valuable insights to traffic authorities. Additionally, frame conversion techniques can be employed to estimate vehicle speed, enabling the system to detect speeding violations and other traffic infractions. By integrating these capabilities, the proposed system aims to improve traffic flow, reduce congestion, and enhance overall road safety.

articleTitle: Analyzing and Forecasting Financial Services using Packet Transform through Wavelet Transitions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Financial analysis plays a pivotal role in understanding market trends and making informed investment decisions. This research leverages the power of Wavelet Packet Transform (WPT) to extract valuable insights from financial time series data. By applying WPT to financial data, complex patterns and trends can be uncovered, enabling more accurate forecasting and analysis. The study utilizes Plotly’s interactive line charts to visualize these insights effectively. The proposed approach has demonstrated exceptional performance, achieving an accuracy rate of ${9 9 . 5 \%}$. This high level of accuracy empowers stakeholders and financial advisors to navigate the dynamic financial landscape with greater confidence. By providing deeper insights into market behavior, this research contributes to improved decision-making and risk management in the financial industry.

articleTitle: GIS and ML Integrated Techniques for Detection of Landslide-Prone Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Landslides are a common natural disaster that can result in substantial casualties. One of the region’s most vulnerable to landslides in India is Western Ghats. The risk casualty is reduced with the use of the landslide susceptibility map (LSM) and prediction of landslide points. The aim of this research is to explore and compare the 4 ML algorithms (K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression (LR)) for generating the most promising LSM. This study focuses on 12 Landslide conditioning factors (LCFs) such as Elevation, Slope, Lithology, LULC, Distance to Road, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), Stream Power Index (SPI), Topographic Roughness Index (TRI), Drainage Networks, NDVI, Rainfall, Sediment Transport Index (STI). It has been found that the slope of the ground, the distance to the road, and the annual rainfall all have a significant impact on the occurrence of landslides. The models made using different approaches have been analysed and compared using the following metrics: prediction accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and True Skill Statistics (TSS). Overall accuracy for LR, SVM, KNN, RF are 82.30, 84.00, ${8 2. 5 0, 8 7. 2 0}$ respectively. The findings of the study show that there are more landslide-prone locations in Bhor, Velhe, Ambegaon, and Junnar in Pune District, Maharashtra.

articleTitle: A Secure Approach for Strengthening Session Management with Custom Session Handlers
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Session management is the underlying security mechanism that is instrumental in protecting the security and integrity of web applications’ user sessions. The research is dedicated to the examination of session administration solutions in web applications to provide secure user sessions and minimize the risks of session hijacking and session fixation. It touches on session management before and after user login, breaking it down into session maintenance. The custom session handler offers passive protection against session hijacking via session management using a MySQL database. This approach provides a safe way of creating and managing sessions, validating them as well as handling session expiration and performance optimization. The implementation intends to strengthen session securities of users, therefore, increasing the safety and reliableness of web applications

articleTitle: Classifying Brain Tumors using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Brain tumors, which develop uncontrollably, are difficult to diagnose, treat, and prognose. Treatment and outcomes depend on early detection and precise classification. This study uses imaging and deep learning advances to compare three state-of-the-art Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) brain tumor classification models: VGG16, InceptionV3, and ResNet50. The Kaggle dataset comprises meningioma, glioma, pituitary tumors, and no tumors. VGG16 was the best performer, with 0.89 accuracy, 0.91 precision, 0.89 recall, and 0.90 F 1 -score, thanks to its simple architecture that captures crucial features. ResNet50 used residual learning to solve the vanishing gradient problem, achieving 0.86 accuracy and a 0.87 F1-score. Despite its novel multi-scale feature extraction, InceptionV3 has an accuracy of 0.74 and an $\mathbf{F 1}$-score of 0.75, possibly due to overfitting. These findings demonstrate VGG16’s applicability for brain tumor detection clinical applications demanding high precision and recall. Advanced data augmentation, regularization, and ensemble methods should be studied to improve complex models like InceptionV3. These CNN architectures could be optimized for clinical brain tumor classification using larger and more diversified datasets. Early intervention and constant monitoring are crucial to brain tumor management and patient quality of life, according to this study.

articleTitle: Analyzing Hydroponic Farming with a Drip System and Comparing it to a Decision Tree (DT) using a Logistic Regression (LR)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This study will assess Decision Tree and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithms’ ability to predict tomato quality, yield, and growth in Deep Water Culture (DWC) hydroponic farming. We evaluate multiple machine-learning methods for hydroponic input prediction. The DWC approach collects data from hydroponic tomato farms. Yield, fruit size, leaf area, $\mathbf{p H}$, water temperature, illumination, and fertilizer concentrations are among these statistics. Key dataset features like growth attributes, environmental impacts, and nutrient concentrations are selected for model training. The result reveals that Decision Tree and SVM can forecast tomato production and growth factors. SVM may be more accurate than a Decision Tree, although the latter is simpler to understand. In tomato yield prediction, SVM is $\mathbf{8 8 \%}$ accurate and Decision Tree $\mathbf{8 5 \%}$. The predicted parameters affect recall and precision; SVM usually has higher precision. Conclusion: Decision Trees and Support Vector Machines can forecast tomato farming results in DWC hydroponic systems. Decision Tree is simpler and interpretable, although SVM is more precise in some cases.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of Large Image Model and Pre-trained CNN for the Classification of White Blood Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: White blood cells (WBCs) must be accurately classified in order to be used in medicine for both therapeutic and diagnostic purposes. The performance of two domains that are very efficient in classifying blood cells are examined in this work, with particular emphasis on the models’ robustness and accuracy of classification. The development of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and, more recently, Large Image Models (LIMs) has drastically changed the landscape of image recognition. This study examines how well these two architectures perform in comparison when used for image-based tasks with uncommon datasets. Although CNNs have proven to be exceptionally powerful in certain fields, LIMs hold the potential to achieve more broad picture understanding. To do this, this research study compares a pre-trained CNN and a cutting-edge LIM. These results clarify the classification of each strategy, showing that CNNs can potentially beat LIMs at jobs requiring specialized expertise. This work adds to the current discussion on model selection in image analysis by highlighting the significance of dataset properties in choosing the best architecture. This research study intends to direct the creation of more efficient image recognition systems for a variety of applications by comprehending the trade-offs between generalization and specialization.

articleTitle: Development of IoT Enabled Aqua Pond Monitoring System to Increase the Livelihood of the Aqua Farmers
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research study aims to eliminate the invasion of the Aqua-life. The proposed system monitors the levels of parameters($\mathrm{pH}, \mathrm{DO}$, etc.) by using IoT devices, such as D18B20 water temperature, which can indicate the temperature of the water body, DO sensor by DFRobot, used to display the dissolved oxygen levels in the lake, turbidity sensor to find the dust dissolved in the water, and finally the pH sensor that can tell us about the nature of the pond/lake, whether it is basic in nature or acidic in nature. All of these sensors are connected to a microcontroller, which is Arduino rev2, that collects the data and sends it to the Blynk, where the data is stored and displayed to the user. The data, that is collected will be the analog values and those values, which are between $0-1023$ will be converted to voltage, where the range will be between 0V and 3.3V or 0V and 5.5V, range will depend on the voltage supplied to the particular sensor. After obtaining the voltage values for the data, which includes the values of pH, DO, turbidity and temperature, these values again undergo a process of conversion, that gives out the sensor’s particular value. All of these sensors or can say the system will be placed on the boat, which can controlled by using a mobile or a computer. Making the boat rover over the water can get us the data, to show that the water body is safe for the aqua-life or it is not. Based on this piscators will take the measurements required to save the harvest, that will be yielded soon or later.

articleTitle: Utilizing Hybrid-Deep Learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection in Children via Facial Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that significantly impacts social interaction and communication. Early detection and intervention are crucial for optimal outcomes. This research investigates the use of deep learning techniques to identify ASD based on facial emotion analysis.
