Core techniques such as spatial and frequency domain processing, multiscale methods, and morphological operations are discussed for their roles in enhancing, transforming, and analyzing images. Furthermore, the research discusses about the influence of deep learning and neural networks, especially CNNs and GANs to transform image analysis and synthesis. Some major areas of application are met emphasizing how image processing technologies foster developments in health care, space science, security, and manufacturing industries. This study also focuses on present issues such as computational complexity, data protection, and data ethics. Future directions and trends are discussed as well as directions for future research, focusing on the prospect of combined use with other future technologies such as AI and IoT. Thus, the goal of this research work is to map out the field of image processing to help practitioners and researchers better understand the current and future state of the field.

articleTitle: Multi-Tier Intrusion Detection System for Underwater IoT Wireless Sensor Networks using Hybrid Machine Learning and Reinforcement Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Underwater IoT wireless sensor network (UIoTWSN) is very important for monitoring and gathering real time data in marine environments. This dynamic and complicated nature of these environments leads way to different security threats like listening in, blocking, forging and flooding. Traditional intrusion detection system (IDS) for UIoTWSN is not better at identifying threats due to many false positives which take long time for computation. An adaptive hybrid deep learning framework for efficient attack detection in UIoTWSN to deal with this problem. This proposed method integrated deep learning and reinforcement learning to create flexible and resilient system. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to select the complex patterns for spatial feature extraction in the underwater network data. Then the temporal feature extraction is handled by Bidirectional Long short-term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and it provides the detailed way of how the network behaves over the time. Then the AdamW optimizer is utilized to make sure that the proposed system works efficiently. This hybrid method employs reinforcement learning to change dynamically to new intrusion patterns and changing underwater conditions. Finally, a multi-tier detection method is made to manage the various types of attacks without any problems. Every tier concern on various threats and it employs unique detection methods. This multi-tier detection method identifies the types of intrusion which makes the UIoTWSN more reliable and stronger. Many experiments shows that the suggested framework is better than the existing methods. With 96.7% of accuracy, 94.5% of precision and 95.2% of memory, this method achieves superior performance. These metrics shows that the framework is better at identifying the intrusions accurately when avoiding the false positives and additional task for the system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Attention-Enhanced Transformer With Modified Graph Cuts (AAET-MGC) Algorithm for Cardiovascular Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: One of the core prerequisites in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases is accurate segmentation of the myocardium walls and small vessels in cardiac MRI datasets. Traditional segmentation methodologies often do not tackle this complexity of cardiac structures and their variability across MRI images. This may further enhance overfitting and local minima problems during training of deep learning models for cardiac image segmentation. Against this backdrop, a new hybrid approach is introduced called Adaptive Attention Enhanced Transformer with Modified Graph Cuts. This methodology is devised to merge the local feature extraction using a Convolutional Neural Network with the global context awareness provided by the transformer encoders further enhanced by attention mechanisms; user interest is oriented toward the most relevant features. The AAET-MGC model integrates an adaptive energy function within a modified graph cuts framework with spatial and intensity information, aiming at refining the segmentation results. This hybrid approach uses the power of deep learning in an initial segmentation process and classical graph cuts for accurate and smooth boundary detection. The method is evaluated against a comprehensive cardiac MRI dataset with an accuracy of 97%, avoiding overfitting and local minima. The AAET-MGC approach outperforms competing methods in the accurate segmentation of thin and complex structures, conductive to better diagnostic accuracy for the related clinical applications.

articleTitle: Virtual Frontiers Navigating the Impact and Potential of AR and VR
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research study aims to investigate the two rapidly growing fields of Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality from their technical aspect, possible uses, issues, and evolution. AR and VR are innovations that have experienced a massive advancement and are prevalent across the entertainment industry and the learning process, healthcare, industries, and more. The study defines the basic concepts and the physical components that form the basis of AR and VR. It then goes over specific examples, using AR in the context of interactive education and its social impact as well as in operations such as surgeries and in factory maintenance while demonstrating the applications of VR in gaming, education and as a therapy tool. A fundamental question of the examined technologies, which is primarily discussed in the paper, includes the distinct challenges it encountered the hardware constraints of the solutions, the problems related to UX and UI, and the privacy-related concerns. Moreover, it covers the morality and social impact of the integration of AR and VR into society. Finally, examining the future directions of the survey, it is revealed that possible technologies and research areas for the next generation of AR and VR applications are discussed. Consequently, this overview seeks to present useful recommendations regarding the current status of four AR and VR technologies and their possible future developments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Customer Behavior Analysis and Segmentation for Personalized Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In today’s competitive e-commerce, gaining insights into consumer behavior is crucial for businesses to thrive. By analyzing customer data, businesses can make informed decisions to optimize marketing strategies, product offerings, and customer experiences. This research implements machine learning techniques to segment customers into distinct groups based on their purchasing behavior. The process involves data preprocessing, feature engineering, and dimensionality reduction to enhance data quality and extract relevant information. K-means and hierarchical clustering algorithms are employed to identify optimal clusters. By analyzing the characteristics of each customer segment, businesses can tailor their marketing efforts and product recommendations to meet the specific needs and preferences of different customer groups. This personalized approach can significantly improve customer satisfaction and drive sales. This study demonstrates the potential of machine learning in unlocking valuable insights from customer data, ultimately leading to improved business performance and customer engagement.

articleTitle: An Attention-based Rainfall Prediction System using LSTM Model and Convolutional Block Module
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: For practical purposes including managing water supplies, building infrastructure, and growing food, rainwater prediction is crucial. Since precipitation time series inherently includes a non-stationary component, the model’s effectiveness is diminished for both practicing hydrologists and prospective drought investigators. A model that predicts the likelihood of rain, based on Deep Learning (DL), was proposed by many researchers as a solution to the weather prediction issue. The need for study into the challenges of short-term rainfall quantity prediction has grown in response to climate change. In particular, the high computing needs and error proneness of the current numerical weather prediction models make them unsuitable for precipitation forecasting. Predicting the quantity of precipitation is difficult because it requires long-term information on many environmental phenomena, including temperature, humidity, wind direction, and more. Three attention models namely Squeeze and Excitation (SE), Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and Convolutional Block Attention (CBA) are utilized with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) in this work. CBA with LSTM performed best in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). CBA with LSTM achieved a very low RMSE value of 0.28 when compared to other attention models.

articleTitle: Digital Integrity: Enhancing Image Forensics with Error Level Analysis and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The widespread use of digitally altered images highlight the need for trustworthy methods to differentiate between real and altered content. This study introduces ELA as a more effective and economical method for detecting changes in digital images, diverging from the original method described in the base work, which employed Fourier transform of residual images. This study offers a reliable method for differentiating between authentic and altered photos using error level analysis (ELA) in combination with a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN), which is MobileNet. The proposed methodology uses ELA to detect faint aberrations suggestive of picture alteration, from which MobileNet extracts significant features in an effective manner. An SVM is then used to classify the collected features, thereby drawing a line between genuine and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated images. The results of the experiments show that the suggested design performs robustly in picture classification tasks, achieving a high accuracy of 94.18%. This research adds to the field of image forensics by improving the dependability of fake image recognition and providing a scalable solution that can be used in a variety of real-world circumstances, such as cybersecurity and content verification. This integration of ELA with SVM and MobileNet is a major step forward in the ongoing actions taken to maintain the integrity of digital media and fight false information.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Object Detection Algorithm for Autonomous Vehicles with Hybrid Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In order to improve accuracy and efficiency in object detection tasks, this research study introduces a novel hybrid object detection deep learning technique that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Support Vector Machines (SVM). The suggested approach combines the strong classification ability of SVMs with the feature extraction capabilities of CNNs to provide a more efficient detection model. To further optimize the performance, a hybrid optimization algorithm is introduced, combining the Hybrid Bat AlgorithmGrey Wolf Optimizer (HBA-GWO) and Aquila Variabilis Optimizer-Particle Swarm Optimization (AVO-PSO). The HBA-GWO algorithm exploits the exploration abilities of the Bat Algorithm and the exploitation capabilities of the Grey Wolf Optimizer to efficiently search the solution space. In contrast, the AVO-PSO hybrid algorithm combines the strengths of the Aquila Variabilis Optimizer’s dynamic search strategies with the Particle Swarm Optimization’s global convergence ability. The integration of these two hybrid optimization strategies aims to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the CNN-SVM model, thereby enhancing detection accuracy and reducing computational costs. Experimental results on standard object detection benchmarks demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed hybrid model in terms of precision, recall, and F1 score and mAP compared to traditional deep learning and optimization methods. This research highlights the potential of hybrid models in advancing the field of object detection through the synergistic combination of machine learning algorithms and optimization techniques.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Real Time Implementation of Automatic Weighing and Packing Machine in Rice Mill
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research study presents an automated material handling and packaging system designed for various rice mill, focusing on its components, operation, benefits, and potential future developments. The system is centered on an Arduino Uno microcontroller board, powered by the ATmega328P chip, which coordinates the functions of several motors and sensors. The core components of the system include a gear motor for generating suction, servo motors for precise positioning and movement control, relays for direction change, and a hopper mechanism for material deposition. After the hopper is filled, the system transitions to the weighing and bag filling stage, where the amount of material is measured and dispensed into bags accurately. This process ensures consistency and accuracy in the filling process, contributing to efficiency and precision in material handling. Furthermore, the paper highlights the advantages of automatic weighing and packing systems, including increased efficiency, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness. These systems streamline operations, reduce labor costs, and enhance overall productivity. They also contribute to improved food safety by minimizing human handling and contamination risks. The integration of automatic weighing and packing systems into rice mills and small industries is seen as promising, offering enhanced efficiency, productivity, and product quality. These systems streamline packaging processes, reduce manual labor, and allow for handling larger volumes of materials with fewer resources. Their scalability and customization make them adaptable to the specific requirements of different industries. In conclusion, automatic weighing and packing systems offer significant benefits to business, including improved efficiency, accuracy, and product quality.

articleTitle: Drone Technology: Revolutionizing Agriculture, Construction, Healthcare, and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: These days, drone technology has come a long way in a variety of fields. After finding widespread employment in the military, drones are already ubiquitous in everyday life, and their potential uses are only going to grow. The attractiveness of drones comes from their remote control capabilities, which allow them to be handled even from great distances and in sensitive locations that humans cannot reach. Equipped with technologies like as GPS, which allow for exact position computations, they communicate data in real-time via satellites. The commercial, healthcare, and military sectors are among the most prominent users of drones, and the market for these aircraft is predicted to expand at a rate of around 15% per year over the next few years. The general atomics MQ-9 REAPER is very efficient in military operations, the DJI MG 1S is ideal for agricultural tasks, and the ZIPLINE FIXED-WING DRONE is ideal for medical applications, among others. Drones like this come in many shapes, sizes, weights, and capacities, and they’re all designed to do specific jobs better. Task execution relies on efficient communication between base stations and drones, which can be achieved using cellular, satellite, or ground mesh techniques. Drones are becoming increasingly adaptable for a wider range of uses as technology works to increase their accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Error Correction and Machine Learning for Robust Optical Fibre Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Optical fibre communication systems are key for high-speed data transmission but they face challenges such as transmission errors and signal degradation. Hence this study proposes an innovative method that combines adaptive error correction technique with machine learning algorithm to enhance the robustness and reliability of optic fibre communication. Adaptive error correction methods are utilized, specifically low-density parity check codes and Turbo codes which are known for their efficiency in handling high error rates in data transmission. These techniques dynamically adjust their error correction parameters based on the different conditions of optical fibre communication channel. Then, the integration of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) are utilized to detect and correct errors in real time. For training and evaluation, the International Telecommunication Union (ITU-T) are employed. This dataset includes different signal parameters and error scenarios. Experimental evaluation demonstrate that this method eliminates the bit error rate and enhance the signal to noise ratio compared to traditional error correction methods. It also ensures minimal latency, making the method suitable for high-speed optical fibre communication system. This study contributes to the field of optical fibre communication by providing a robust solution that utilizes the strengths of both adaptive error correction and machine learning.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for Predicting Nitrate Concentration in Groundwater
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This study focuses on water quality assessment in the Dharmapuri district, specifically within the Karur taluk region, with a particular emphasis on total nitrogen concentrations. Water samples were collected and analyzed for total nitrogen content, and the outcomes were compared to the Water Quality Index (WQI) and World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. The optimal WQI value for water quality is 100, whereas the WHO limit for total nitrogen in drinking water is $10 ~\mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L}$. The global challenges posed by poor drinking water quality necessitate urgent attention due to the impacts of developmental activities, pollution, and climate change on water resources. Different levels of contamination were highlighted by the analysis, which showed values ranging from $5 ~\mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L}$ in Mampatti to $180 ~\mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L}$ in Elavadai. Various machine learning models, including, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting, and Neural Networks were employed for predicting nitrate concentrations. Comparative analysis revealed that while Neural Network and SVM models tended to underestimate, especially at higher concentrations, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest models produced predictions that were more in line with real nitrate levels. These patterns were supported by scatter plots comparing real and predicted values for SVM and neural network models, which showed the methods’ limits in capturing the whole range of nitrate variability. This research highlights the need for enhanced prediction models to guarantee efficient management of groundwater quality and focused approaches to reduce nitrate pollution in the area.

articleTitle: EOG and PPG Fusion for Subject Independent Multimodal Emotion Recognition: A Prototypical Networks Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition is recognizing the emotion from more than one modality like facial expression, gestures, speech, text and physiological signals. The prototypical networks is a well-known few-shot distance based machine learning algorithm, in which data point is classified based on the proximity to the prototype. In this work, the prototypical network algorithm is modified for multimodal emotion recognition using EOG and PPG, in which Smooth L1 loss is explored for learning the embedding space. This study also explored correlation, Euclidean, squared Euclidean and chord distance as distance metrics to learn the embedding space. The proposed method obtained a prediction accuracy of 60.00% and 61.00% in arousal and valence dimensions respectively which is higher than the accuracy reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Back Propagation Model Based Machine Learning In Feed Forward Neural Networks for 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The creation and use of 6 G technologies are anticipated to heavily use machine learning. There are a number of ways that machine learning may boost 6G, even if research and standardization are still in their early phases. Real-time network resource allocation may be made more efficient by using machine learning methods. In order to ensure effective resource utilization and enhanced network performance, this also involves dynamic spectrum allocation, power regulation, and network slicing.To improve spectrum efficiency, 6G is anticipated to make use of improved beamforming techniques and huge multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) devices. Beamforming pattern optimization, channel condition adaptation, and capacity enhancement can all be aided by machine learning methods. To allow wise choice-making for base station installations, interference control, and user association, machine learning may be applied to the RAN. This improves network coverage, lowers latency, and improves user experience. This paper demonstrates the training of a basic feed forward neural network using the back propagation method. The network is trained by applying the back propagation technique through the execution of the train function. After making predictions on the test set using the trained network, evaluation measures like accuracy and root mean squared error (RMSE) are calculated.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Mango Leaves Disease Detection for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Several diseases impact the mango crop, lowering yields and lowering fruit quality. Because of economic hardship and inadequate medical facilities, many nations still struggle with the diagnosis of these illnesses. Several strategies for the automated identification of mango illnesses have been developed by researchers in the recent decade. The suggested system for detecting mango leaf diseases uses improved deep learning methods to identify the root causes of the diseases and provide recommendations for their treatment. To detect diseases in images of mango leaves, the suggested study uses Tensor Flow. The proposed method employs the identification of items API tensor flow to independently diagnose illnesses; it is trained using a convolutional neural network (CNN). This research study has developed advanced transfer learning models using the VGG-19, ResNet101, and InceptionV1 topologies to detect mango diseases from pictures of healthy and diseased leaves. The proposed approach outperforms its predecessors with a 95.2% accuracy rate in illness leaf identification.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective EMG Signal Acquisition for Rehabilitation Robotics using Single-Channel Sensors and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Electromyography study focuses on the classification of electromyography (EMG) signals using machine learning (ML) techniques. The classification of EMG signals with ML techniques improves the response and accuracy of myo-electric prosthetic hands and rehabilitation systems. One of the key techniques to get reliable surface EMG signals is to employ multiple sensors. Integrating multiple sensors in myoelectric hands can inflate the cost of prosthetic hands. To study the effectiveness of implementing a single sensor combined with machine learning algorithms to accurately classify the EMG signals, an experiment was conducted and reported in the paper. EMG signals were collected from five volunteers to create a comprehensive dataset. Various machine learning algorithms were then applied to classify the EMG data effectively. The proposed approach achieved an accuracy of over 80%, highlighting the potential of using single-channel EMG sensors combined with machine learning for accurate signal classification. This approach could be beneficial for various applications, including prosthetic control and rehabilitation devices.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Generation from Speed Breakers for Smart Street Lighting Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research explores the potential of integrating rack and pinion mechanisms with electromagnetic induction to generate electricity for street light control systems. By converting mechanical energy into electrical energy, this approach offers a sustainable and environmentally friendly solution. The proposed system utilizes Light Dependent Resistors (LDRs) and a Raspberry Pi microcontroller to dynamically control street lights based on ambient light conditions. This intelligent control strategy optimizes energy consumption and reduces operational costs. This research study analyzes the theoretical foundations, design considerations, and implementation methodologies of the proposed system. Experimental validation demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of the approach. By promoting the use of renewable energy sources and reducing reliance on conventional power grids, this innovative solution contributes to the development of sustainable and resilient urban infrastructure.

articleTitle: IoT based Automatic Fertilizer Mixer and Sprinkler System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In the traditional agriculture system, the farmers are analyzing the temperature, soil moisture, soil fertility, and plant nutrient availability, which are the climate and soil variables that most growers pay the most attention to. Farmers find that applying fertilizer and irrigation using traditional methods takes a lot of time. Energy and water consumption in farming can be increased by over-irrigation, fertilizer leaching below the root zone, erosion, and the movement of soil and chemical particles to the drainage ditches. Farming will be far less expensive and time-consuming with a single system that combines fertilization and irrigation. Granular and watersoluble fertilizers are the two types of fertilizers offered to home gardeners. Granular fertilizers often release nutrients more gradually than water-soluble fertilizers, but they can also last longer. This work will create an automated system for fertilizing and watering plantations using a NPK sensor to determine the amounts of potassium (K), phosphorus (P), and nitrogen (N). The microcontroller is an Arduino. The information is then processed by the microcontroller, which also controls the irrigation and fertilization pumps that provide the field’s sprinkler system with water and fertilizer. The user will receive any input via the system. On the other hand, manual or conventional field management of these variables will not give producers a clear picture of the amounts available to meet plant requirements according to developmental stages. Therefore, the most effective use of inputs, such as water and fertilizers, will be made possible by continuous automated monitoring and control of these soil nutrient elements, ensuring high crop production potential while upholding safe environmental conditions. The purpose of this work is to develop an automated sprinkler and fertilizer mixer system based on the internet of things (IoT) that will benefit farmers in terms of time and cost.

articleTitle: Dynamic Weather Prediction: Real-Time Analysis using Deep Learning Techniques and Live Data
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: We have long been used to checking the weather every day to organize our thoughts and make plans for a few daily tasks, trip plans, or anything else we need to accomplish. This may be done purposefully or accidentally to monitor the weather. People used to measure the weather in the sky in the distant past. Later, they started using disobedience to predict the weather in a community. Climate estimates for portable phones had then arrived. That means that people also develop and use climate figures on a daily basis. Verifying the average weather can let everyone go about their lives without any uncomfortable influences, such as intense downpours or chilly breezes. Most of the time, the reason we selected this is to examine the average weather may help everyone go about their lives without any uncomfortable influences, such as intense downpours or chilly breezes. Our decision to look into this topic is usually based on how important it is to each person’s daily existence. In this study, we looked at several methods for estimating climate and how to calculate it. However, the main focus of our analysis is the Long Short-Term Memory, or LSTM, calculation that we selected to provide a workable climate estimate. For real-time weather analysis, this project integrates LSTM networks with a relational database called MySQL. Large amounts of weather data are effectively stored using MySQL, and precise forecasting is achieved via LSTM through analysis of past data. SQL queries are used in the cooperation to extract and preprocess data. Analytical comparisons show that the system outperforms conventional techniques and provides higher temporal pattern accuracy. This integration has the potential to revolutionize sectors that depend on accurate weather data because of its modular architecture, which guarantees adaptation to a variety of areas and weather conditions.

articleTitle: A Systematic Survey on Diabetic Retinopathy and Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a significant threat to the vision of human beings; it is affected by patients and needs to be detected in the early stage to reduce the severity of vision. In recent research, the DR become interdisciplinary medical and computer science research. In this paper, based on the importance of this research, our research systematically reviewed the deep learning algorithms for automated DR detection, highlighting datasets, model implementations, and challenges. The study explored the Deep Learning approaches in DR management by assessing performance and clinical importance. In this review, our research also included the comparative study of various model outputs based on the different datasets, needful preprocessing techniques, and model refinement for accurate DR detection. We also discussed the integration of advanced models into clinical practice to improve DR management and reduce vision loss associated with diabetes. DR remains a significant global health problem, and advanced detection methods are used to mitigate vision loss. This literature review systematically examines the role of DL algorithms such as EfficientNet and MobileNet in enhancing DR detection. Through rigorous analysis of IDRiD (Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset) datasets, model implementations, and challenges, the study synthesizes current research to explain critical directions and understandings. Our research concluded that integrating Deep learning into clinical research holds a guarantee for improving the accuracy and efficiency of DR detection, thereby improving patient results and quality of life. This review delivers valuable wisdom for researchers and clinicians aiming to advance DR detection methodologies and implement innovative solutions for this condition’s early diagnosis and management.

articleTitle: Detection and Mitigation of Vampire Attacks in Wireless Sensor Networks using Weighted Hopfield Neural Network with Nature Inspired Optimal Path Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) consist of several nodes whose primary objectives are to monitor and regulate surroundings. Furthermore, sensor nodes are distributed in accordance with network utilization. The energy consumption of sensor nodes is one of the most important problems in this kind of network. In fixed-sink networks, nodes in close proximity to the sink serve as intermediaries for transmitting data from other nodes to the sink. This results in a significant decrease in sensor energy usage. Consequently, the network’s lifespan decreases. Due to their vulnerabilities, sensor nodes are prone to various attacks, including the vampire attack that poses a danger to WSN. This paper presents a novel approach for the detection and mitigation of vampire attacks using a Weighted Hopfield Neural Network (WHNN) combined with bio-inspired optimal path selection. The WHNN is employed to detect abnormal energy consumption patterns indicative of vampire attacks, leveraging its associative memory capabilities. To counteract the detected attacks, we incorporate a bio-inspired optimization algorithm, such as Aquila optimizer Algorithm (AOA), to dynamically select the most energy-efficient paths for data transmission. This dual-layered strategy not only enhances the detection accuracy of vampire attacks but also ensures optimal path selection. Due to their vulnerabilities, sensor nodes are prone to various attacks, including the vampire attack that poses a danger to WSN. The superiority of the WHNN-AOA technique is proved by simulation results, when compared to current schemes, based on performance measures such as packet delivery ratio, average throughput, detection ratio, and network lifespan, while also reducing the average residual energy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Robust Object Detection in Weather-Impacted Environments using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)

authors.preferredName: M V T Ram Pavan Kumar

abstract: This research study presents R-YOLO (Robust You Only Look Once), a robust object detection framework designed to address weather-related issues. R-YOLO makes use of the YOLO architecture and incorporates additional features to lessen noise and increase visibility in the event of adverse weather. Adaptive filtering and a weather-aware attention mechanism are two of these features. By combining conventional datasets with a well annotated weather-specific dataset, the model is trained on a sizable dataset that spans a variety of weather conditions. According to the trial results, R-YOLO outperforms both baseline YOLO models and state-of-the-art detectors under adverse weather conditions, exhibiting more adaptability and generalizability. Furthermore, real-time applications like robotics, autonomous driving, and surveillance are suitable for R-YOLO. The proposed framework not only maintains good performance in a variety of adverse weather conditions but also improves object detection accuracy in low visibility scenarios, making it a dependable and useful choice for real-world implementation. This paper investigates the potential benefits of R- YOLO for computer vision applications, particularly in situations where adverse weather poses significant challenges.

articleTitle: FTTA: Optimizing Resource Utilization in Cloud Environment using Meta-Heuristic Scheduling Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In Cloud Computing (CC) environment, optimizing resource utilization is critical for enhancing performance, reducing energy consumption, and minimizing operational costs. This paper introduces a novel Football Team Training Algorithm (FTTA) designed to improve resource allocation and utilization in dynamic cloud environments. Inspired by the collaborative and strategic dynamics of football team training, FTTA models tasks as players, assigning them to available cloud resources based on real-time workload and performance metrics. The algorithm effectively balances exploration and exploitation, ensuring that resources are allocated optimally while minimizing underutilization or overloading. Simulation results demonstrate that FTTA improves resource utilization by 20.6%, reduces task completion time by 16%, and enhances throughput by 18.4% when compared to traditional algorithms. These improvements make FTTA a promising approach for cloud service providers aiming to optimize resource management and deliver superior quality of service (QoS).

articleTitle: Object Detection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), more often known as drones, have lately gained significant attention in the aviation sector because of the vast variety of potential applications they might have in areas such as surveillance, environmental monitoring, agricultural, and disaster management. The evolution of UAV-based object identification systems is the subject of this article. A better and faster way to recognize and categorize items from aerial photography is to combine UAV technology with advanced Computer Vision (CV) algorithms. The research explores several strategies, focusing on Deep Learning (DL) frameworks like Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) and region-based approaches. It emphasizes how well these frameworks perform and adapt in complex and dynamic contexts. Issues with data transmission, real-time processing, and the impact of UAV flying characteristics on detection performance are also included in the study. The results indicated that object detection systems using UAVs have great potential to enhance situational awareness and decision-making in many different domains, which might lead to new developments and uses in the future.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction Unveiled: Analyzing the Effectiveness of RandomForest, LogisticRegression, and KNeighbors
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research explores the application of three distinct machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and KNeighbors—to predict software faults. These algorithms are evaluated using various performance metrics, including Accuracy, F1 Score, Precision, Recall, and ROC AUC, to assess their effectiveness in identifying software defects. Random Forest, known for its ensemble learning approach, combines multiple decision trees to improve prediction accuracy. Logistic Regression, a statistical model, is used for binary classification tasks, offering insights into the likelihood of faults occurring. KNeighbors, a non-parametric method, classifies instances based on their proximity to other data points. Each algorithm is scrutinized for its ability to accurately forecast software issues, providing a comprehensive evaluation of how well it can differentiate between faulty and non-faulty instances. The comparative study reveals the strengths and limitations of each model. Random Forest may excel in handling complex relationships and interactions between features, while Logistic Regression provides a straightforward, interpretable approach. KNeighbors can be effective in capturing local patterns but may struggle with large datasets. Understanding these nuances helps in selecting the most appropriate model based on specific benchmark evaluation cases, which is critical for enhancing fault prediction performance. This research underscores the importance of choosing the right model for software defect prediction. The findings indicate that different algorithms offer varying advantages depending on the context and evaluation criteria. Consequently, future work in this area should consider these insights to refine fault prediction methods further. The paper provides a foundational guide for future research, highlighting the need for tailored model selection and evaluation strategies to improve software defect prediction accuracy and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Optimizing Climate Data Classification with a Novel Ensemble-based Stacking Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This research explores the novel machine learning model using stacking classifier with ensemble learning for climate data classification. The proposed model systematically integrates various machine learning techniques, encompassing crucial phases including data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model stacking. By leveraging a combination of logistic regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost and Random Forest models, this research paper demonstrates how ensemble approaches can effectively capture complex patterns within climate data. The dataset, sourced from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) data repository of hurricane data, includes a wide array of features related to hurricanes and tropical storms, making it ideal for analyzing and predicting storm status. The use of a Stacking Classifier combining multiple models (logistic regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost) appears to be quite effective, achieving 95.74% accuracy, outperforming individual models and simpler ensemble methods. The research establishes the prospective of machine learning techniques to improve climate data analysis and prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Predicting Sham Claims in Vehicle Insurance using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The insurance industry is experiencing rapid growth and as a result, faces the challenge of managing vast amounts of data. One of the foremost concerns within this sector is the issue of fraudulent claims, which refers to deceptive attempts made for personal financial gain. This deceitful practice affects both insurance companies and their honest policyholders due to the prevalence of such claims. Traditionally, domain expertise and conventional methods have been employed to detect fraudulent activities in insurance claims. However, more recently, data mining techniques have emerged as valuable tools in the field of insurance analysis. These techniques enable the calculation of insurance premium amounts and the prediction of both fraudulent claims and accident occurrences. The premium amount is determined based on individual customers’ confidential and financial information. Implementing this research significantly reduces human effort and financial losses in the examination of automobile insurance claims. Effective classifiers play a crucial role in determining whether a claim is fraudulent or not. Predicting the occurrence of accidents is a fundamental step in identifying fraudulent claims. Decision tree classifiers, such as Simple CART, SVM, and LMT, available in the WEKA tool, are employed to analyze accidents and claims. The execution of these classifiers is compared in terms of accuracy, with Random Forest demonstrating superior accuracy in predicting accident occurrences and yielding the best results among the classifiers. Furthermore, the SVM algorithm outperforms other classifiers in predicting fraudulent claims.

articleTitle: Vision Beyond the Haze: Advancements in Cataract Detection and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Eye diseases are among the most critical health issues impacting human life. One of the most frequently encountered eye problems is cataracts, due to which people suffer as they age. The cloudiness that forms on eye lenses is known as cataracts which can significantly damage vision. Diagnosing the disease in its acute stage rather than its onset should not blind the patient. This study presents an improved Cataract detection method using pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on an Ocular Disease Intelligent Recognition (ODIR) dataset, Comparing the performance of ResNet50, ResNet101, and VGG19 architectures to find the most effective model for this project. The proposed approach uses deep learning to analyse fundus images, aiming to increase diagnostic accuracy, speed, and reliability. several preprocessing and data Augmentation techniques were utilized to prepare the data set, which provided robust training and improved model generalization. Samples were refined using pre-trained ImageNet weights and adjusted for binary classification of Cataract presence. Among the tested models, ResNet50 exhibited the best performance, achieving an overall accuracy of 99.08% It also showed good evaluation metrics, with a precision rate of 98.15% and 100% recall for cataract images, and 100% precision with 98.23% recall for normal images. The results highlight the potential of ResNet50 to provide accurate and effective cataract diagnosis, especially in areas where access to trained ophthalmologists is inaccessible. This study highlights the importance of using deep learning technologies to improve the early detection and treatment of cataracts, ultimately contributing to better patient outcomes and global eye health progress.

articleTitle: Prediction of Groundwater Potential Mapping using Linear Regression and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Groundwater capacity studies assess subsurface resources using multiple methodologies. Groundwater mapping potential estimates can help manage and schedule resources. Finding good groundwater development locations is essential for sustainable management. Geological, hydrological, and environmental data are needed to map underground water potential. Water resource management and hydrogeology can influence groundwater mapping potential. Several methods have been used to predict groundwater potential mapping. This study estimates groundwater potential using genetic algorithms and linear regression. The recommended linear regression approach estimates groundwater potential and parameters. Select the most critical groundwater potential variables and optimize the linear-regression model. Groundwater mapping potential is predicted after model optimization. An area with different hydrogeological parameters was examined to test the approach. The proposed method accurately predicts groundwater potential mapping and provides relevant water resource management data. LR-GA helps manage water assets and calculate groundwater potential. The advice is 93.7% correct. The proposed approach is ${9 0. 6 \%}$ sensitive and ${8 9. 6 3 \%}$ specific.

articleTitle: Enhancing Overvoltage Resistance in Electrical Feeders: A Case Study on CEPALCOs Pueblo de Oro Feeder 2 with Critical Node Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Lightning strikes are prevalent on the overhead distribution lines of CEPALCO’s Pueblo de Oro Feeder 2, often causing significant insulation damage and leading to partial or total system shutdowns. While lightning arresters are considered an effective solution to this problem, they require significant investment, making large-scale use across CEPALCO’s extensive network economically unfeasible. In response to this challenge, this study explores a Critical Node Optimzation technique known as Direct Discharge Crossing (DDC). This method is used to efficiently place lightning arresters, ensuring adequate protection for the distribution system while minimizing cost. Simulations were conducted using EMTP-RV, a power system analysis software, to model the CEPALCO PDO F2 feeder. The results of the study demonstrate that installing lightning arresters at the most critical positions significantly reduces flashover incidents and decreases the D function for each pole, leading to enhanced system reliability and reduced maintenance costs. This approach offers optimal resource allocation and improved lightning performance of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Investigation of 3D Printed Lithophane Quality Improvement on A FDM Printer
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In recent years, the process of creating lithophanes has involved the use of 3D printing technologies to produce transparent plates of varying thicknesses and when backlit, these lithophanes create images. The process includes building a 3D model of the lithophane with open-source 3D modeling software. Then, the print parameters are chosen, and white PLA filament is used for printing. This research investigates the optimization of 3D-printed lithophanes on Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM). Using Taguchi’s DOE approach, five key parameters such as brightness, contrast, maximum thickness, minimum thickness, and vector per pixel were chosen, and each was investigated at three distinct levels. A total of 27 samples were systematically designed and printed to examine the impact of these parameters on the quality of 3D-printed lithophanes. The Python script was used to analyze the experimental data and find the best set of parameters to enhance the lithophanes’ visual appeal. The results of this investigation provide significant contributions to the field of 3D printing, particularly with regard to the production of visually engaging and captivating lithophane prints through the use of FDM technology.

articleTitle: Review of Battery Thermal Management System: Role of PCM in Thermal Management
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of electric vehicles (EVs) is contingent upon the development of efficient and reliable battery technologies. Thermal management plays a crucial role in optimizing battery performance, extending its lifespan, and ensuring safe operation. This research study reviews various temperature control techniques employed in Battery Thermal Management Systems (BTMS), including air cooling, liquid cooling, and phase change materials. These techniques aim to maintain optimal operating temperatures, prevent thermal runaway, and enhance overall battery performance. By effectively controlling the battery’s temperature, BTMS can significantly improve the vehicle’s range, charging speed, and safety. As battery technology continues to evolve, the importance of thermal management will remain paramount in shaping the future of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: BLOA: Optimizing Resource Utilization using Multi-Objective Task Scheduling in Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The Butterfly Lion Optimization Algorithm (BLOA) is proposed as an innovative hybrid metaheuristic approach for Task Scheduling (TS) in Cloud Computing (CC) environments. Proposed algorithm is combination of mating and foraging behaviour of Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA) and hunting strategy of Lion Optimization Algorithm (LOA). TS is a critical challenge in CC, where the goal is to efficiently allocate resources while optimizing multiple objectives such as minimizing makespan, reducing execution time and response time while maximizing the throughput. The BLOA combines the dynamic exploration capabilities of butterfly behavior with the strategic hunting techniques of lions, creating a robust algorithm that balances global exploration and local exploitation. This hybrid algorithm leverages the strengths of both butterflies and lions to navigate complex, high-dimensional search spaces typical of CC environments. By integrating adaptive mechanisms, the BLOA is capable of dynamically adjusting to varying workload demands and resource availability. Comparative evaluations against other leading scheduling algorithms demonstrate that BLOA achieves superior performance in terms of reducing makespan time by 18.15%, execution time by 11.23%, and response time by 14.78%, while maximizing the throughput by 21.11%. The algorithm is especially useful for CC environments that are heterogeneous and distributed, which makes it ideal for cloud service providers who intend to improve resource utilization as well as decrease energy consumption and operational costs.

articleTitle: Forecasting Renewable Energy Generation: A Predictive Modelling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: India’s rapid urbanization demands innovative solutions to address energy consumption patterns while reducing reliance on fossil fuels. This research paper explores the application of predictive modelling techniques like Multilayer Perceptron and Polynomial Regression to forecast solar energy generation and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to forecast wind energy generation, thereby facilitating efficient energy planning in major Indian cities. The proposed system aims to create a web-based platform that integrates these predictive models to display real-time temperature conditions and the corresponding amount of energy that solar and wind sources can provide in specific locations, thus promoting smart cities and smart homes. By utilizing the website, energy planners will be able to compare the generated energy from wind and solar sources, enabling informed decisions on which resource best meets the energy requirements of housing settlements.

articleTitle: Skill Adam Optimization based Deep Spiking Neural Network for Retinal Multi Disease Classification in Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The aim of fundus imaging is to inspect the irregularities corresponding to diseases that affect eye. The fundus image has a crucial role in detection and observation of diverse ophthalmic diseases. Existing researches have engaged on detection of single disease from the fundus image. However, simultaneous recognition of multi-disease (MD) from the fundus images is still confronting a major challenge. Therefore, this challenge can be addressed by devising a model to detect MD from the fundus imaging with an enhanced accuracy. Here, Skill Adam Optimization based Deep Spiking neural network (SAO_Deep SNN) is introduced for retinal MD classification using fundus images. Initially, considered fundus image is pre-processed to eliminate noises utilizing Median filter (MF). Thereafter, optic disc (OD) is segmented by DeepJoint segmentation and next, artery and vein (A/V) classification is accomplished using sparking process. Then, features are extracted from OD segmented image and A/V classified image in feature extraction (FE) phase. Finally, retinal MD classification is done by Deep Spiking Neural Network (Deep SNN). However, Deep SNN is trained utilizing Skill Adam Optimization (SAO) that is introduced by integrating Skill Optimization Algorithm (SOA) with Adam algorithm. Additionally, SAO_Deep SNN achieved accuracy of 90.81%, sensitivity of 91.69% and specificity of 90.49%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) often struggle to effectively address the evolving landscape of cyber threats. This research explores the potential of machine learning techniques to improve the accuracy, speed, and adaptability of IDS. This research study reviews various machine learning approaches, including classification, regression, clustering, dimensionality reduction, semi-supervised, and reinforcement learning, and their application to intrusion detection. Effective data preprocessing and feature selection techniques are crucial for optimizing the performance of machine learning models. The evaluation of IDS performance is discussed, focusing on metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC-AUC. The challenges associated with low-quality data, computational complexity, and adversarial attacks are highlighted, along with potential future research directions. By integrating machine learning, IDS can be transformed into more intelligent and adaptive systems, capable of detecting and responding to advanced cyber threats. This research contributes to the advancement of cybersecurity by providing a comprehensive overview of machine learning techniques and their application to intrusion detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Virtual Try-On: A Study of Methodological Innovations and Dataset Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The research proposes a framework for virtual try-on that addresses the limitations of existing methods by incorporating advanced techniques in computer vision and machine learning. The proposed approach leverages a deep convolutional neural network architecture to effectively model the complex interactions between clothing items and human bodies. To address this, numerous researchers have zeroed in on developing intelligent apparel systems, particularly image-based virtual fitting solutions. However, these systems face challenges due to variations in poses, occlusions, and lighting conditions. While significant progress has been made in image-based virtual fitting systems, their effectiveness is often hindered by the limited availability of clothing data, particularly traditional attire from diverse cultures. To address this limitations arising primarily from insufficient datasets, the following endeavor proposes a groundbreaking approach that aims to overcome these challenges and provide more inclusive and accurate virtual try-on experiences.

Author Keywords: High-Resolution Virtual Try-On via ALIAS Normalization (VITON-HD)

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Automatic Epilepsy Detection Techniques: Problems and Limitations
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Recurrent seizures are a hallmark of the neurological illness epilepsy, which presents formidable diagnostic and therapeutic obstacles. There is significant potential for newly created automated seizure detection systems that use Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) approaches to improve patient care and expedite intervention. Electroencephalograms (EEGs) are a mainstay in the diagnosis of epilepsy, and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) have lately gained prominence due to their ability to mimic temporal correlations in sequential data. Recent advances in automated epilepsy diagnosis using ML and DL are thoroughly covered in this work. The current research goes over the use of RNNs in seizure detection using EEG data and the several RNN designs that may be used for this task, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bi-Directional Long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). This research takes a look at several problems and limitations associated with ML and DL-based approaches, including data scarcity, inter-subject variability, and the interpretability of models. Additionally, the current research emphasizes potential avenues for further study that might strengthen and improve ML and DL-based systems for epilepsy diagnosis, such as eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods, transfer learning, and multi-modal data fusion. Together, the study’s results and suggestions illuminate two very important areas: automated epilepsy diagnosis based on ML and DL and their current and future state of development.

articleTitle: Multilingual Toxic Comment Classification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Toxic comments can have a profoundly negative impact on online communities, fostering environments that feel unsafe, unwelcoming, and discouraging for participation. The task of toxic comment classification focuses on identifying and categorizing harmful or disruptive comments within online discussions. Despite extensive research in this area, several challenges persist, such as Multilingual Toxicity Detection, Data Imbalance, and Interpretability. Existing studies have categorized toxic comments into six distinct labels: toxic, severely toxic, obscene, threat, insult, and identity hate. Traditional machine learning models like SVM have achieved an accuracy of 87%, while more advanced models like BERT have reached up to 98.3%. The goal of this proposed work is to improve the identification of toxic comments across multiple social media platforms, particularly in datasets containing entries in multiple languages. To address this, deep learning models such as XLM-RoBERTa and BERT are employed to detect the language of the comment and classify it as either toxic or non-toxic. Each model’s performance will be evaluated primarily using Accuracy metrics, providing a basis for comparison to determine the most effective approach for multilingual toxic comment detection. High accuracy can be achieved through careful dataset preprocessing, advanced model architectures, and hyperparameter tuning. Performance can be improved by fine-tuning model hyperparameters and employing better feature extraction techniques. More clarity is required in explaining the rationale behind selecting particular models.

articleTitle: A Critical Review of Road Accident Prediction and Analysis Techniques, Data Sources, Challenges and Opportunities in Future Developments
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In today’s era, road accidents are highly increasing across world, leads to cause severe injuries and death on every year. It has also imposed with economic loss, financial crisis for the society. Day by day, the road accident occurrence remains as an inevitable factor. Therefore, the accident prediction model is required to develop and deploy for evading such kind of calamities. Researchers have focused on designing a significant impact of model for analyzing the road accident scenarios. It is accomplished with the help of standard techniques, algorithms. Despite many techniques have explored, the victims count is increased. Also, the identification of cause for road accident is quite challenging task since it holds with large dimensional data or depends with one or multiple factors. As traffic accidents caused by various reasons, the rising of automated model becomes the best solution. In such way, enormous techniques have been implemented to reach the best value as well. Over the decade, the research is going on deeper to forecast the accidents that can influence with the risk of traffic rules and facilities. In this survey, different and existing road accident prediction models are analyzed. For better presentation, the road accident and its problem are given. Several learning methodologies are used for the purpose of enhancing the prediction performances that is also to be analyzed. The prediction techniques suggested for identifying the road accidents in the existing research works is analyzed and categorized. Different types of performance metrics used to verify the performance of each prediction model in existing literatures is checked. Future developments are discussed to improve the capability of road accident prediction models.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models for Stock Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The stock market has always been evolutionary. It has been an area of interest for researchers to forecasting the stock prices too guide investment decisions and avoiding financial risk since many years. This paper highlights the significance of precise stock price prediction and investigates the use of several machine learning techniques to strengthen the predictive accuracy. The proposed system makes uses two different approaches: Regression, which predicts the company’s stock closing price, and Classification predicts whether the closing price of the stocks will increase or decrease the next day. Historical stock data is examined carefully and preprocessed to ensure high quality of data. Using feature engineering appropriate features are extracted to identify the intrinsic patterns and trends within the stock market. Algorithms like Linear Regression, ARIMA, LSTM and Random Forest are implemented and thoroughly evaluated for their efficiency in stock price prediction. After conducting a comparative analysis of the two algorithms, it becomes evident that while LSTM performs exceptionally in regression tasks, identifying the temporal associations and patterns that guide the stock market data in its development, Random Forest provides more firm predictions of the stock price movement. This study provides the extensive analysis of the real-life application of machine learning for discussions on the stock market, thus allowing investors to derive a more reliable resource to refer to when dealing with the challenges of the stock market.

articleTitle: Integrating Deep Learning with Case-based Reasoning for Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Detecting brain tumors (BT) early is vital for effective treatment planning and improved patient outcomes. The fusion of Deep Learning (DL) and case-based reasoning (CBR) presents a promising solution for enhancing BT detection accuracy and reliability. DL methods, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), excel in automatically extracting discriminative features from medical images, bolstering diagnostic capabilities. Case-based reasoning, on the other hand, leverages past diagnostic cases to provide context-aware decision support for new cases. This review study provides an overview of recent advancements in the integration of DL with CBR for brain tumor detection. Then discuss the strengths and limitations of both approaches and highlight how their integration can address key challenges in brain tumor detection, such as limited labeled data, interpretability of DL models, and the need for personalized diagnosis. Furthermore, review existing studies that have applied DLand CBR techniques individually and in combination for brain tumor detection. Finally, discuss challenges and future research directions and opportunities for leveraging this integrated approach to improve brain tumor diagnosis and patient care. In this, review total 55 papers are taken based on the Integrating DL with Case-Based Reasoning for Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection. In this, the research articles published between 2021 and early 2024 were taken into consideration for this study.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance using Machine Learning for Industrial Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In recent years, the fourth industrial revolution has drawn interest from all across the world. Many concepts emerged from this new revolution, one of which being predictive maintenance. Predictive maintenance can be achieved for industrial machines through implementation of machine learning techniques to monitor real-time operational data. It can analyze sensor data for early prediction of equipment failures and to reduce downtime and optimizes scheduled maintenance. The purpose of this investigation is to look into developments in academic failure prediction. Predicting failures involves taking into account ideas such as design support systems and predictive maintenance decision support systems. The research gap is identified by analyzing the existing literature studies by exploring optimization strategies through integration of predictive maintenance in industrial environment in smart factories.

articleTitle: Secure Sentiment Analysis of Stock News Via Blockchain-Integrated Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative method to tackle the complexities of ensuring secure and verifiable sentiment analysis of stock news using a combination of blockchain and federated learning integration. The proposed hybrid framework connects recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for sentiment analysis. It employs blockchain-based smart contracts for model verification, thereby upholding the confidentiality and integrity of the federated learning process. Within the federated learning network, each participating node independently trains a local RNN model on its specific set of stock news articles, protecting data privacy. The accumulation of model updates is achieved through secure federated averaging, and the blockchain network consensus mechanisms validate the authenticity of the aggregated model. Automating the verification process via smart contracts allows only valid updates to be accepted and recorded on the blockchain ledger. The transparency and immutability of the blockchain enable stakeholders to scrutinize the federated learning procedure and ensure the dependability of the sentiment analysis results. Our approach is assessed through simulations and experiments, illustrating its efficacy in maintaining data privacy, preventing adversarial attacks, and imparting confidence in the sentiment analysis of stock news.
